name: Epidemiology
notes: Thirteen required courses plus two recommended mathematics courses. The major leads to a BA and satisfies the social sciences requirement of the Rochester Curriculum.
RECOMMENDED (not required): MATH 161 and MATH 162, or the MATH 141-143 sequence.
Prerequisites of the individual courses are not counted toward the major.

PHLT 102 (Introduction to Public Health II) stopped being a required course in spring 2024 and is no longer offered. Students already declared in the EPD major continue on the program they declared under; anyone who completed PHLT 102 intending to use it should ask the undergraduate public health program to incorporate it.
STAT 212 was valid until spring 2024; STAT 180 is the current introductory statistics course (valid from fall 2024).

PM COURSE NUMBERING: the department page writes the School of Medicine courses with a 'U' suffix (PM 412U, PM 414U, and so on) but the catalog and the other public-health programs in this planner carry most of them without it (PM 412, PM 414, PM 418 and its W section PM 418W). The catalog form is used here so a course placed for one public-health program is recognized by the others; PM 415U keeps its U because that is the form the catalog carries. PM 413 (Field Epidemiology), PM 442 (Nutritional Epidemiology) and PM 470 (Environmental and Occupational Epidemiology) appear in no harvested schedule at all.
No more than TWO courses may overlap between a public health major and another major. The introductory STAT course (STAT 212 or STAT 180) is not counted in that overlap.
Students may major, OR minor, OR complete a cluster within the public health-related programs - but not more than one of those.
Students may use up to two transfer courses toward the program with their public health faculty advisor's approval, and up to two PHLT internship courses toward the major.
GROUP III ELECTIVE: the same course may not satisfy both a Group I or Group II elective and the Group III elective. The groups below do not share courses, which matches that rule.
PHLT 397W (Community Engagement Internship) is open to juniors, seniors, Take 5, and e5 public health majors and requires the permission of an EPD faculty advisor.
For each PM (W) course there is a cap of five students who can register for the writing component - register early for the W section.

requirementGroups.label: Public health general core
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Public Health General Core (Four Courses): PHLT 101: Introduction to Public Health I; PHLT 103: Concepts of Epidemiology

requirementGroups.label: Introductory statistics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: STAT 212: Applied Statistics I (valid until spring 2024) or STAT 180: Introduction to Applied Statistical Methodology (valid beginning fall 2024)

requirementGroups.label: Public health or medical ethics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: PHIL 228 (PHIL 228W): Public Health Ethics or PHIL 225: Ethical Decisions in Medicine

requirementGroups.label: Epidemiology core
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Specific Core Requirements (Four Courses): PM 414U: History of Epidemiology; PM 415U: Principles of Epidemiology; STAT 216: Applied Statistical Models I; STAT 218: Categorical Data Analysis

requirementGroups.label: Group I: epidemiology electives (three)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Electives (Five Courses) I. Epidemiology (3 courses). Choose three of the following: PM 412U: Survey Research; PM 413U (H): Field Epidemiology; PM 418U (W): Cardiovascular Epidemiology; PM 424U (W): Chronic Diseases Epidemiology; PM 442U (W)(H): Nutritional Epidemiology; PM 451U (W): Epidemiology of Infectious Diseases; PM 470U (W): Environmental and Occupational Epidemiology; PM 489U (W): Injury Epidemiology and Emergency Care Research Methods; BST 465: Design of Clinical Trials; EESC 251: Introduction to Geographic Systems; PHLT 201W: Environmental Health; PHLT 397W: Community Engagement Internship
requirementGroups.note: W sections are listed alongside their base courses; take the W section of two of these to satisfy the major's writing requirement.

requirementGroups.label: Group II: statistics elective
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: II. Statistics (1 course). Choose one of the following: MATH 218: Intro to Mathematical Models in the Life; MATH/STAT 201: Introduction to Probability; MATH/STAT 203: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics; STAT 217: Applied Statistical Methods II; STAT 219: Nonparametic Inference; STAT 221W: Sampling Techniques; STAT 276: Statistical Computing in R; STAT 277: Introduction to Statistical Software and Exploratory Data Analysis
requirementGroups.note: MATH 201/STAT 201 and MATH 203/STAT 203 are the same cross-listed courses.

requirementGroups.label: Group III: one further epidemiology or statistics elective
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: III. Additional Epidemiology or Statistics Elective (1 course). The same course may not be used to satisfy a Group I or Group II elective course and a Group III elective course.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two upper-level writing courses within the major
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Upper-Level Writing Requirement: Students are required to register for two upper-level writing courses within this major. The courses designated with (W) have writing requirements that would satisfy the Rochester Curriculum's upper-level writing requirement. Students should register for the "W" section; for each PM (W) course there is a cap of five students who can register for the writing component.
